story.title: Narek's story
paragraphs: Narek lives with his family in the Aragatsotn region of Armenia. He took his first steps at one year old, and for the next few years nothing seemed wrong.

When he was about five, his parents noticed that something was not right. He tired quickly, found stairs hard, could not squat or jump, and had to push himself up with his hands to get up from the floor.

Blood tests showed creatine kinase, an enzyme that leaks out of damaged muscle, at more than 11,000 U/L. The normal level is below about 200. In April 2024 a genetic test in Moscow found a deletion of exons 46–48 in his DMD gene, and specialists at the Children's Neuromuscular Centre confirmed the diagnosis: Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
Since then Narek has taken a steroid every morning to slow the disease down, and his doctors have prescribed daily exercise and physiotherapy.
story.today: Narek's condition is currently stable. He can still walk, but he can no longer climb stairs. He goes to school and stays active with sport.
story.parentsMessage: Narek is a brave and kind boy. He goes to school, loves sport, and keeps going even on the days when his legs let him down. Every day we watch him work hard for things other children do without thinking, and we know that time is not on our side. Elevidys is the first real chance to slow his illness down and help him keep walking for longer. We cannot afford it on our own, so we are asking for your help. Every donation and every share brings Narek closer to that chance. Thank you from the bottom of our hearts.

dmd.title: What is Duchenne muscular dystrophy?
paragraphs: Duchenne is a rare genetic disease that affects about 1 in every 3,500 to 5,000 boys. A fault in the DMD gene means the body cannot make dystrophin, a protein that protects muscle fibres. Without it, muscles are damaged every time they work and are slowly replaced by fat and scar tissue.
There is no cure. Steroids and physiotherapy slow the disease down, but they cannot stop it.

timeline.text: First signs: frequent falls, trouble with stairs and with getting up from the floor.
Weakness grows. Steroids and physiotherapy help to slow it down.
Most boys lose the ability to walk and need a wheelchair.
Weakness reaches the arms, the heart and the muscles used for breathing.

treatment.title: The treatment: Elevidys gene therapy
paragraphs: Elevidys (delandistrogene moxeparvovec) is a one-time gene therapy developed by Sarepta Therapeutics. It is given as a single infusion into a vein. It carries a shortened but working version of the dystrophin gene into muscle cells, so that the body can start making a protective protein called micro-dystrophin.

Elevidys is not available in Armenia. It is approved in the United States and in several other countries, including the United Arab Emirates, where Medcare Royal Speciality Hospital in Dubai has accepted Narek as a patient.
treatment.eligibility: Before treatment, every patient is tested for antibodies to AAVrh74, the modified, harmless virus that carries the gene. Narek's test was negative. On 17 August 2026 Dr Vivek Mundada, consultant paediatric neurologist at Medcare Royal Speciality Hospital, confirmed that he is clinically suitable for the therapy.
treatment.whyNow: The therapy is given to boys who can still walk, and it can protect only the healthy muscle that remains. Antibody results can also change over time. Every month of waiting matters.
treatment.honestTitle: What the treatment can and cannot do
treatment.honest: Elevidys is not a cure. It is designed to slow the loss of muscle strength and help Narek stay on his feet for longer. Like every gene therapy, it carries risks, including serious liver injury, so his doctors will monitor him closely before and after the infusion.

items.q: How can I be sure this is genuine?
items.a: All of Narek's medical documents are published on this page. You can confirm his eligibility with Medcare Royal Speciality Hospital in Dubai (medcare.ae), and you can contact the family directly using the details below.

items.q: Why does the treatment cost so much?
items.a: Elevidys is one of the most expensive medicines in the world. In the United States a single dose has a list price of about 3.2 million US dollars, before hospital, travel and follow-up costs.
Elevidys is not available in Armenia. It is approved in the United Arab Emirates, and Medcare Royal Speciality Hospital has reviewed Narek's case and accepted him as a patient.
No. There is no cure for Duchenne yet. Elevidys is designed to slow the disease down so that Narek keeps his strength and stays on his feet for longer.
